review.title: Two Tits, Two Owls
review.headline: Both cats claimed roles that were already taken, and both got caught fast.
review.summary: Casey's Hawk egg pinned Drew in the first beat of Round 1. Drew winked Casey anyway, then gave himself away by calling himself "Mouser-free". In Round 2 Finley the Sphinx claimed Owl, but the real Owl, Drew, outed him straight away. Finley then found a real lie, Casey's Hawk claim, but only after the day had ended. Alex was Farm in both rounds and held a 13 to throw, so he won 46 to 38. Finley was Meowfia twice and finished with 7.

rounds.recap: Casey the Hawk visited Drew and gained an egg. Ellis's Falcon info backed this up, and Blair's confused Kookaburra read also said Drew was a cat. Drew winked Casey, which took 5 votes off the count. Drew still lost 9 votes to Finley's 1 and was eggsecuted, and Casey still banked 37 while dead.

Finley claimed Owl, and Drew, the real Owl, counter-claimed with a result that backed up Ellis's Tit claim. Three CAWs came in beat 2. Finley's true point that Hawk wasn't dealt, so Casey was lying, came too late. Finley took 4 votes and was eggsecuted.

highlights.text: Alex and Finley both claim Tit, and Alex correctly calls Finley a liar.
Drew winks his main accuser Casey, then says he is "Mouser-free Farm" and gives himself away.
Drew counter-claims Owl with a result that confirms Ellis's Tit, and the table piles onto Finley.
Finley uses his Sphinx info to show Casey's Hawk claim is impossible, one turn after the day had already ended.

confusions.what: His Sphinx info showed a real Tit was in play, but he claimed Tit anyway and walked into a counter-claim.
Said he 'didn't get visited by a Tit' as proof. A Tit doesn't learn its visitors, and a wrong Tit guess gives no egg anyway.
Claimed Owl when he knew Owl was in play. He also said Alex, Casey and Ellis 'lost eggs', but their nests were small because they threw cards in Round 1.

Said Casey couldn't have visited him because he visited Casey. Visits aren't exclusive, and a Tit can't see its visitors. He also said Finley's nest 'went up 1'. It actually went from 5 to 7 through the normal 2-card deal.
Called Finley's 7 cards suspicious, but those were cards left over from Round 1.
Asked who visited Finley because Finley had 7 cards. That was leftover cards, not night eggs.
Also called Finley's 7 cards odd when they were just leftover cards.
His private reasoning had Casey's Hawk egg coming from 'another Meowfia' when Casey had actually visited Drew himself.

design_notes: Hard confirmations ended both rounds by beat 2. A Hawk egg plus a visible nest count is close to proof, and so is an Owl counter-claim. The cats never got a real chance to bluff.
Nests carry over between rounds, but the day listing shows only raw sizes. Four players took leftover cards for night eggs. Show each nest's change since the round's deal.

Golden Wattle never mattered. There was one offer, from a cat, and it was refused. The -3 penalty gives Farm players no reason to offer or accept. Consider a reward for proven same-side bonds, or a smaller cross-team penalty.

The Wink was weak. Casey died but still banked 37 points. Drew was eggsecuted anyway, and the kill made him look guilty. Consider making dead players' throws not score, or using the Wink before throws are locked.

Which team you got decided the winner. Finley was Meowfia twice and scored 7. Alex was Farm twice, had a 13 to throw, and won. With only 2 rounds and a one-card consolation for the losers, being Meowfia is close to an automatic loss. Also, players in the same group could speak after the CAW, so Finley's best evidence arrived after the day had ended.
